messages:
emma ng: Heads up — after the checkpoint-2026-03 merge we're seeing a steady p99 latency regress on staging (around +40-60ms). Started at ~09:12UTC during canary traffic.
raj patel: which path? generation, embeddings, or rerank?
emma ng: generation. Pre-tokenize and KV cache warmup look suspect. p50 flat, p99 up.
taylor chen: I pulled a flamegraph, looks like spike in kernel selection hotpath and allocator churn when kvcache misses happen.
maria gonzalez: do we have a CI perf job that caught this?
ci-bot: [perf-check] staging/push at 09:08 — p99 regression detected: +52ms vs baseline (master@f3a2c). Link: https://ci/redwood/perf/2629
raj patel: ok repro steps? can you paste the minimal repro or a perftrace?
emma ng: ran a short synthetic load: 1000 requests @10 TPS, seq len 128. Attached the tail logs:
```
[09:12:21] request id=abc123 kernel_select: chosen="matmul_fallback" score=0.12
[09:12:21] kvcache: miss key=tokmap_202603 checkpoint=2026-03
[09:12:21] allocator: spin wait 12ms alloc_size=48KB
[09:12:22] request id=abc124 kernel_select: chosen="matmul_optimized" score=0.11
```
taylor chen: hmm kernel_select choosing fallback for the first chunk then optimized for subsequent ones — looks like selection heuristic is oscillating because tokenizer output changed length distribution.
maria gonzalez: tokenizer change in the new checkpoint? There was a subtle pretokenize normalization tweak in model package.
raj patel: tokenizer length shift would change batch packing and prefetch heuristics. KV keys are different so warm cache miss rate spikes. That explains alloc churn as we hit more cold paths.
ci-bot: Note: the onboarding job for checkpoint-2026-03 passed functional tests but did not run the long perf sweep (was skipped due to quota).
ops-bot: Rolling back would affect release schedule. Consider a targeted canary pause.
emma ng: I started a bisect on the commit range that landed tokenizer normalization + kernel selector heuristics tweak. Early signs point to the tokenizer update as trigger.
taylor chen: can you dump a comparison of token lengths for the same corpus between master and checkpoint-2026-03?
emma ng: pasted small sample stats:
```
master: avg_len=14 median=9 tails>64=0.6%
checkpoint-2026-03: avg_len=17 median=12 tails>64=1.8%
```
raj patel: tails tripling explains more KV churn and occasional long allocations due to bigger KV frames.
maria gonzalez: quick mitigation: pin tokenizer normalization to previous behavior in the onboarding config, re-run perf sweep.
emma ng: tried that locally — p99 drops back to baseline but kernel selector still shows a few misroutes on mixed inputs.
taylor chen: I hacked kernel selection rule to include a token-length bias (if avg_len>15 prefer optimized kernels) and ran a micro-benchmark — p99 returned to baseline at 2k RPS.
raj patel: that's promising as a short-term hotfix. But we need a proper solution: either update batching heuristics to be length-aware, or add a warmup step for KV prefetch during onboarding.
emma ng: creating a rollback patch and a kernel-selector patch. Patch links: https://phab/r/1321 (rollback tokenizer), https://phab/r/1322 (selector bias).
ci-bot: perf-run queued for rollback patch. ETA ~15m.
ops-bot: Can we pause the global rollout of checkpoint-2026-03?
maria gonzalez: I've paused canary >50% traffic. Notifying infra.
taylor chen: for post-mortem: add a perf-gate to onboarding that runs a short seq-length sweep (16/32/128/256) and KV miss profiler. Also a KV-key stability check.
emma ng: agreed. I'll add to the onboarding checklist and add an e2e perf job.
raj patel: action items: 1) rollback tokenizer normalization (emma) 2) land kernel selector bias short-term (taylor) 3) add onboarding perf sweep (maria) 4) update docs for KV key changes (raj)
emma ng: landing rollback now. will update when CI green. :pray: 
ci-bot: [perf-check] rollback patch landed, CI perf: p99 delta +3ms vs baseline (within noise).
maria gonzalez: unpause canary when rollback fully rolled out.
ops-bot: canary traffic resuming at 09:58UTC.
taylor chen: follow-up: I'll prototype a more robust batching heuristic that uses a short windowed token-length histogram to avoid mid-request kernel oscillation.
emma ng: thanks all. filing a short postmortem draft.
raj patel: please include the token-length diffs and flamegraphs. Good catch on KV warmup.
emaria gonzalez: (typo correction) maria gonzalez: I'll own the onboarding perf job implementation.
ci-bot: [incident] resolved — root cause: tokenizer normalization increased token length tail and caused KV cache cold misses + kernel selection oscillation; mitigated by rollback and selector bias patch.
